chunks: Allāh the Glorified, the Sublime, created (the things of) creation. He created them without any need for their obedience or being safe from their sinning, because the sin of anyone who sins does not harm Him nor does the obedience of anyone who obeys Him benefit Him. He has distributed among them their livelihood, and has assigned them their positions in the world.
ai.seo_question: What does it mean that Allah is independent of human obedience and sin?
ai.summary: This passage elucidates the Shia theological concept of divine self-sufficiency (Al-Ghani), affirming that God’s essence remains unaltered by human deeds, a principle that underscores the wisdom behind His distribution of rizq (livelihood). It reflects the Imami understanding that worldly stations are not rewards for piety nor punishments for sin, but manifestations of His sovereign will and justice. This perspective distinguishes between God’s ontological independence and His relational attributes as perceived by creation.
